- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. - Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

# Long Term Vision + Goal

This project explores the most efficient ways to run a variety of AI/LLM generations on **Vulkan** using the AMD AI MAX+ 395 "Strix Halo" platform, with gfx1151 and RDNA3.5. 

Ultimately we want to be able to run these tasks:
  1. Speech to Text via Nvidia's `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3`:
    * https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2509.14128v2
  2. Text generation via Qwen's `Qwen3.8-Next-Flash`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30320v1
    * We'll need to quantise the weights once we've determined the most efficient method for the hardware
  3. Text to Speech via Hexgrad's `kokoro-82M`:
    * https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2306.07691v2
  4. Image generation and editing via Qwen's `Qwen-Image-2.1`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1
    * https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1
    * Unified text-to-image and reference-image editing (up to 10 refs), native RGBA transparency
    * In-progress previews: no tiny autoencoder exists yet for its 64-channel VAE,
      so we fit our own linear preview and watch https://github.com/madebyollin/taehv
      for a proper one (replaced z-image-turbo + taef1 on 2026-09-20; plan in IMAGE.md)
  5. Compute embeddings via Qwen's `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05176v3

We will ultimately serve up a HTTP API serving these features, in Go.

101	
102	## The model, as the checkpoint describes it
103	
104	Three components, ~32.3 GB on disk (bf16), against Z-Image's ~20 GB resident:
105	
106	| | | |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| DiT | `QwenImage21Transformer2DModel` — **32 single-stream blocks**, dim 4096 (32 heads x 128), SwiGLU **12288** (mlp_ratio 3), **no biases anywhere**, per-head-dim q/k RMSNorm (eps 1e-6), 7.1 B params | 14 GB |
109	| Text encoder | **Qwen3-VL-8B** (`Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`): text model 36 layers, hidden 4096, 32 q / 8 kv heads of 128, theta **5e6**, vocab 151936; plus a 27-layer vision tower (hidden 1152, patch 16, spatial-merge 2, deepstack taps at layers 8/16/24) | 17 GB |
110	| VAE | `AutoencoderKLQwenImage21` — Wan-lineage causal-3D residual conv AE, encoder base 96 / decoder base **144**, dim_mult [1,2,4,8,8], **z_dim 64, 16x spatial**, **4-channel RGBA in and out**, per-channel `latents_mean/std` (64 values each) | 1.3 GB |
111	
112	Geometry: **one latent token = one 16x16 pixel tile** (patch_size 1, VAE /16).
113	Pixel sides must be multiples of **32** (the VLM groups latent tokens 2x2).
114	1024² = 4096 image tokens — the same DiT sequence length as Z-Image at 1024².
115	2048² (the model's native size) = 16384. Defaults: **40 steps, no CFG**
116	(`true_cfg_scale=1.0`; true-CFG exists but is off by design), pipeline default
117	resolution **1024²** (the README's examples use 2048² explicitly).
118	
119	### The four mechanisms that make it different from Z-Image
120	
121	**1. One joint sequence, block-causal.** Text embeddings and image latents
122	share a single stream. The mask is `(q_idx >= kv_idx) OR same_image_block`:
123	the sequence is causal, text tokens strictly so, but every image block (each
124	condition image, and the target) is internally bidirectional. In diffusers the
125	non-flex processor decomposes this exactly into one attention call per prefix
126	segment (text segments get a causal triangle) plus one full-attention call for
127	the target — that decomposition, not a masked kernel, is the shape we port.
128	
129	**2. `causal_condition` + prefix KV cache.** Text and condition-image tokens
130	are modulated from **t = 0** (the modulation tensor carries batch+1 rows; the
131	target's tokens read their sample's row, everything else reads the t=0 row).
132	That makes the prefix's activations step-independent, so **step 0 runs the
133	full block-causal prefill and stores per-layer post-RoPE K/V for the prefix;
134	steps 1..N-1 recompute only the target's tokens**, attending over
135	[cached prefix K/V ++ fresh target K/V] with no mask at all (batch 1, no
136	padding). For t2i the prefix is just the prompt (tens of tokens — small win);
137	for edits it is thousands of tokens per reference image (large win). Caching
138	on/off changes rounding, not correctness — diffusers documents that the two
139	settings give *visibly different but equally valid* samples. **We ship
140	cache-on and validate against diffusers `use_kv_cache=True`.**
141	
142	**3. Sequence assembly and RoPE.** The VLM sequence's `<|image_pad|>` slots
143	each stand for a **2x2 group of latent tokens**: the transformer expands those
144	positions four-fold and drops VAE latents into them; the target's slots are
145	appended after the text. Text embeddings pass through `txt_in` (zero-centered
146	RMSNorm → 4096→4096 → GELU-tanh → 4096→4096); latents through `img_in`
147	(64→4096, no bias). RoPE is 3-axis (frame/h/w, dims 16/56/56, theta 10000),
148	complex adjacent-pair rotation — **the same pairing as Z-Image's DiT**, not
149	the NeoX halves of the text encoder. Text advances all three axes together;
150	each image block freezes the frame axis and lays h/w out on a **zero-centered
151	grid with negative indices** (a flipped negative-frequency table serves
152	indices −1024..−1); after an image block the position cursor advances by
153	`max(h, w)`.
154	
155	**4. Shared modulation.** One `SiLU → Linear(4096→16384)` for the whole
156	model — blocks own no adaLN parameters. Each block chunks it into
157	(scale1, gate1, scale2, gate2); gates pass through **tanh**; norms are plain
158	non-affine LayerNorm. Final head: scale-only AdaLN + `proj_out` 4096→64.
159	Timestep embedding: sinusoidal 256 (cos first half — Z-Image convention
160	differs, check the dump), then a bias-free MLP to 4096.
161	
162	### Text encoding, exactly
163	
164	Raw template strings, **not** `apply_chat_template` (the two tokenize
165	differently and the checkpoint expects the raw form):
166	
167	```
168	t2i:  <|im_start|>system\nComprehend and analyze the provided prompt.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\n{prompt}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n
169	edit: same, with "<image1><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>" (then " <image2>…" etc.) prefixed to the user text
170	```
171	
172	- The embedding is the **last decoder layer's output *before* the final
173	  RMSNorm** (all 36 layers run — different from Z-Image's `hidden_states[-2]`
174	  where the last layer never ran). transformers 5.x silently normalizes
175	  `hidden_states[-1]`; diffusers neutralizes that with a forward hook on the
176	  final norm, and Q0 **verified the hook on transformers 5.17.0**: the hooked
177	  `hidden_states[-1]` equals the pipeline's output exactly (gap 0), so 5.17
178	  is the dump env — the model card requires >= 5.17 anyway.
179	- Drop the first `drop_idx` tokens, where drop_idx = length of the tokenized
180	  system message (computed, not hardcoded). Empty prompt becomes `" "`.
181	- For edits, condition images additionally go through the vision tower (RGBA
182	  flattened over white **for the vision copy only**); mrope with real 3D
183	  positions at image slots. Text-only prompts make mrope collapse to standard
184	  NeoX RoPE — **verified in Q0**: the model's own cos/sin tables for a text
185	  prompt match a plain theta-5e6 table to 0.0 (`mrope_gap` in the textenc
186	  manifest), so nothing mrope-shaped is needed before Q8.
187	- A fact Q8 rests on, confirmed while building the head dump: **the VLM's
188	  image-slot embedding rows are overwritten by the VAE latents** in the joint
189	  stream. Vision content reaches the DiT only through what the *text* tokens
190	  absorbed from the image inside the text encoder's own attention. The vision
191	  tower conditions the text; the VAE conditions the pixels.
192	
193	### Scheduler
194	
195	FlowMatchEulerDiscrete with **dynamic shifting**: sigmas `linspace(1, 1/N, N)`,
196	`mu` linear in the **target** token count between (256, 0.5) and (8192, 0.9)
197	— at 1024², mu = 0.6935, and **unclamped past 8192**: 2048² extrapolates to
198	mu = 1.3129 (measured, Q0) — `time_shift_type: exponential`,
199	`shift_terminal: 0.02`, `stochastic_sampling: false`. Port from diffusers'
200	scheduler, not from Z-Image's fixed shift 3.0. The scheduler steps **only the
201	target latents** (the model's output rows for the prefix are discarded).
202	VAE decode applies `z * std + mean` per channel; encode the inverse, and uses
203	the **posterior mode** (`argmax`), which keeps our seed-reproducibility rule
204	for free.

208	## What this changes about the vertical (semantics, not code)
209	
210	- **Edits stop being SDEdit.** Today an edit is a truncated generation
211	  (strength ⇒ steps skipped ⇒ cheaper). In 2.1 an edit is a *conditional
212	  generation*: reference latents + vision context as prefix, target from pure
213	  noise, all 40 steps. An edit becomes **slightly more expensive** than a
214	  generation (bigger prefix), the `strength` knob disappears, and up to **10
215	  reference images** arrive (OpenAI's `image[]` array already allows several).
216	  `/v1/images/edits` keeps its shape; its documentation changes meaning.
217	  **Measured, Q8.6**: 2m8s against a generation's 1m38s at 1024² with one
218	  reference, `strength` is a 400 explaining the change, and how many
219	  references a given server takes is `-edits N` and `max_reference_images`.
220	- **RGBA is native.** The VAE emits 4 channels always; transparency is asked
221	  for in the prompt (the model card's recommended phrasing). Map OpenAI's
222	  `background: "transparent"` to that prompt prefix + PNG-with-alpha out;
223	  opaque requests composite over white.
224	- **Masked / annotated local edits** (circles, painted regions, separate
225	  masks) are a *capability the model has* — the current 501 for masks may
226	  become closable. How a separate mask is fed (extra condition image?) is not
227	  in the diffusers PR; needs the examples repo before promising it (open
228	  question Q-o3).
229	- **The cost profile inverts — now measured, no longer estimated.**
230	  Z-Image-Turbo was an 8-step distillation at 14.3 s an image; 2.1 wants 40
231	  steps, and Q4's GPU DiT measures **2.27 s a cached step, 2.29 s the
232	  prefill: 90.7 s of transformer per 1024² image** (the morning's estimate
233	  said ~70 s; the gap is unported fusions and the full-seq re-pack, priced
234	  under Q9). **Q6 measured the whole thing served: 1m38.2s / 1m41.3s at
235	  1024²/40** — 92% the denoising steps, 7.6% the VAE, 0.1% the text encoder.
236	  Q9's two priced VAE ports would take the decode from 7.5 s to ~1.3 s, i.e.
237	  the image to ~92 s; everything past that is the DiT's.
238	  2048² is not reachable at all today — the VAE's arena ceiling is 1184²
239	  (Q6) — so the DiT's x4/x16 estimate for it is moot until that is lifted.
240	  The two levers, in order: **the step count** (sweep 40/24/16/12 for
241	  quality — the knob exists, and at 2.27 s/step it is the difference between
242	  ~90 s and ~27 s) and **a distilled/turbo release or LoRA** (the ecosystem
243	  — lightx2v etc. — is where Z-Image-Turbo itself came from; watch for it).
244	  **Q6's sweep decides the served default**; 1024²/40 is the starting point,
245	  not a commitment.

461	  **Gate** (`TestServedOracle256`), both regimes as the rule asks: fed the
462	  oracle's own final latents, our decoder lands the image at **max abs
463	  2.0e-5**; run free from the oracle's noise — the served path exactly, fp16
464	  through 36 encoder layers and 32 DiT blocks — the image is **max abs
465	  0.0333, mean 3.4e-4** from the fp32 reference, which is 1.5x Z-Image's
466	  *fp32* end-to-end precedent on a path that narrows everything. Latents
467	  track at rel 0.0088 over the four steps. **The free-run eyeball Q4
468	  deferred is passed**: `out/qi21served/served1024_40steps.png` is a
469	  photorealistic fox.
470	  **The step sweep settles the default at 40, and finds the failure mode is
471	  the prompt, not the count** (`TestStepSweep`, same seed, three prompt
472	  kinds, PNGs in `out/qi21served/`):
473	
474	  | steps | wall | photographic | painterly | structured/technical |
475	  |---|---|---|---|---|
476	  | 40 | 1m38–1m42 | good | good | good |
477	  | 24 | 1m4 | good | good | good |
478	  | 16 | 44–45 s | good | good | **washed out, structure fragmenting** |
479	  | 12 | 35–36 s | good | good | **broken — the mechanism comes apart** |
480	
481	  A fox photograph and an impasto harbour are convincing at **12 steps**, at
482	  36 % of the cost. A bicycle drivetrain diagram is coherent at 24 and has
483	  disintegrated by 12 — floating parts, ghosted tubes, contrast collapsing
484	  toward white. So **the served default stays 40**, the checkpoint's own,
485	  because it is the only count safe across prompt kinds; **24 is the honest
486	  fast setting** (−35 %, no visible loss on any of the three) and belongs in
487	  the docs as such; 16 and below are a per-prompt choice the `steps` field
488	  already exposes. The pixel distances the sweep also reports (mean
489	  0.025–0.068 against the 40-step image) are **not** the judgement and say
490	  so in the test: fewer steps integrate a different trajectory rather than a
491	  worse one, so the number moves even where the eye sees no loss.
492	  One thing no step count fixed: the diagram prompt asked for "labelled
493	  parts" and got none at 40 either. Prompt adherence on rendered text is
494	  untested territory — Q1 priced an fp32-activation GEMM arm for the encoder
495	  against exactly this symptom and did not build it; if text turns out to
496	  matter, that is the known lever.
497	
498	  **RGBA is served.** `background: "transparent"` is OpenAI's field and it is
499	  answerable because the VAE is natively 4-channel — but it is not a mode:
500	  the server prepends and appends the model card's own recommended phrasing
501	  and keeps the alpha plane, while `opaque`/`auto` composite over white.
502	  Transparent + JPEG is a 400 naming both fields.
503	  **Two capabilities regressed with the model.** `stream: true` was closed
504	  the same day by Q7 (below) and previews are now unconditional. Editing
505	  (Q8) is still refused, naming the stage: `-edits` is a startup *error*
506	  rather than a flag that quietly does nothing.
507	  **The ceiling is a number, and it is not 2048²**: the VAE's activation
508	  arena is one storage buffer, this device caps one at
509	  `maxStorageBufferRange` = 4 GiB − 4, and the decode needs **3060 MB at
510	  1024², 4090 MB at 1184² and 4315 MB at 1216²** (`TestArenaCeiling`). So
511	  **1184² is the largest square this decoder decodes**, against a model whose
512	  own README examples are 2048². `pipeline.New` refuses a larger ceiling with
513	  the arithmetic *before* staging 27 GB (`TestGeometryCeiling`). Closing it is
514	  a capability, not a percent, and there are two routes: tiled decode (what
515	  diffusers' `enable_tiling` does, and the up blocks are local enough for it)
516	  or splitting the arena across several buffers bound as a descriptor array —
517	  `vk.PipelineSpec.Counts` already exists for exactly this, and the LLM's
518	  77 GB bank is the precedent.
519	  **Amended 2026-09-21 (Q10): that ceiling is an *area*, and shipping it as a
520	  pair of side limits was costing every non-square request 44% of its
521	  pixels** — see the stage below.
522	  **The Z-Image deletion is half done, on purpose.** Gone: `zimage/dit`,
523	  `zimage/pipeline`, `cmd/zimage`, `cmd/ditstack`, `cmd/ditbench`,
524	  `cmd/ditblock` — nothing else imported them and `qimage/` replaces all of
525	  it. **Kept for now: `zimage/vae`** (decoder, encoder, both GPU paths,
526	  `tiny*`) and `cmd/vaebench`/`vaedecode`/`vaeprof` with it, because
527	  `gpu_conv.go` is the *validated test bed* for the one kernel Q9 wants —
528	  `TestGPUConvMatchesScalar` proves the matrix-core convolution against a
529	  scalar oracle, and deleting it before Q9 has taken the packing helpers
530	  across would throw away the proof and keep the problem. It goes when Q9
531	  lands. `zimage/qwen` and `zimage/tokenizer` stay permanently (`embed`,
532	  `llm`, `parakeet` and `qimage` all import them).
533	  **The 62 GB of weights on disk are not deleted** — `models/Z-Image-Turbo`
534	  and `models/taef1`. Nothing in the tree reads them now, so it is one
535	  command whenever you want the space back, but it is not a change worth
536	  making on a machine's behalf.
537	- **Q7 — previews. Done 2026-09-20** (`qimage/pipeline/preview.go`,
538	  `preview_matrix.go`, `cmd/previewfit`). `stream: true` and
539	  `partial_images` answer again, and the regression Q6 recorded is closed.
540	  **The decoder is one 64x4 matrix and a bias** — 260 float32s compiled in,
541	  least-squares fitted. A preview decode measures **159 µs against a 587 ms
542	  step (0.03%)**, and three partials over HTTP cost **0.3%** of the request
543	  (10.27 s against 10.24 at 512²/16) — against Z-Image's 4.4% through taef1.
544	  That is why **previews are not behind a flag any more**: `-preview` and
545	  `-previews` are deleted, not repurposed. Under Z-Image they bought 1.0 GB
546	  of activation arena; here there is nothing to load.
547	  **The fit** (`cmd/previewfit`) generates its own pairs rather than reading
548	  Q0's two: it runs the served pipeline over 24 prompts chosen to span
549	  colour and content — primaries, skin, foliage, night, snow, flat graphic
550	  colour, neutral greys — at 512²/8 steps, box-filters each 16x16 image
551	  block onto the latent pixel that produced it, and solves one 65x65 normal
552	  system with four right-hand sides. 24576 samples for 260 parameters.
553	  The shipped matrix is fit on all 24 prompts and scores **R² 0.969–0.974
554	  on RGB** (rms 0.098–0.114 in [-1, 1], 12–15 of 255 8-bit levels).
555	  **`-report` is the honest number**: holding the last six prompts out
556	  entirely gives **R² 0.83–0.90 on unseen content** (rms 0.176–0.198). The
557	  gap is real and is what a 260-parameter linear map costs — six held-out
558	  prompts are six palettes it never saw — and it is the right order for a
559	  latent2rgb preview, whose job is composition and colour rather than
560	  fidelity. Alpha is near-constant on opaque prompts, so its R² (0.63 train,
561	  0.26 held out) over an rms of 0.0014 means nothing; it is reported rather
562	  than hidden.
563	  **The tensor decoded is the denoised estimate x0, not the sample** — the
564	  schedule is flow matching, so ten steps into forty the sample is still
565	  three quarters noise. `Run` forms it after the Euler move, where the
566	  identity is x0 = x_{t+1} − σ_next·v and needs no copy of the pre-step
567	  latents. `TestPreviewFrames` carries that as a **negative control**:
568	  decoding the sample instead is 2.5x further from the finished image at
569	  step 0 (0.394 against 0.157), and the two are asserted *identical* at the
570	  last step, where the terminal sigma makes them the same quantity.
571	  What a preview cannot do is resolve what the latent does not carry
572	  per-pixel: it is 1/16 scale with no texture, upscaled by whatever displays
573	  it. What it carries is composition, colour and layout — at 512²/16 the
574	  first frame lands at **2.27 s against a 10.25 s image**.
575	- **Q8 — edits. Done 2026-09-20**, in six sub-stages: the reference and the
576	  vision tower, the edit text encoding, the CPU pipeline with its resampler
577	  and GPU VAE encoder and GPU tower, the GPU edit text encoding, the GPU DiT
578	  edit path, and the served pipeline with its endpoint. The
579	  stage is (a) VAE encoder serving reference latents, (b) the vision tower,
580	  (c) the multi-image template, mrope with real 3-D positions and deepstack
581	  injection, (d) the pipeline and the endpoint. `/v1/images/edits` drops
582	  `strength` and gains multi-ref.
583	  **Less of it was new than the plan assumed.** The DiT side — per-reference
584	  RoPE blocks, the segments, the prefix cache across refs — was already
585	  ported *and gated* by Q2 against the synthetic edit case in
586	  `out/qi21dit`/`out/qi21block` (≤4e-5, both regimes), and `dit.NewLayout`
587	  already takes a list of image shapes. Q5 built the VAE encoder. So (a) and
588	  (c)'s DiT half were done before this stage opened.
589	  **Q8.0 — the reference. Done** (`reference/dump_qi21_vision.py`,
590	  `out/qi21vision`): 50 tensors over two deterministic RGBA cards, a 256²
591	  one and a 192x384 one, two runs byte-identical. It walks the processor's patching, the interpolated
592	  position grid (indices *and* weights, as the model computed them), the
593	  vision rope table, every block the deepstack taps, the three deepstack
594	  features, the merger, the 3-D mrope position ids, and the pipeline's own
595	  `prompt_embeds` and `image_pad_mask`. It also pins the fact Q8 rests on,
596	  at gap **exactly 0**: the merger's rows are what the encoder scatters into
597	  the `<|image_pad|>` slots, and the DiT then overwrites those rows with VAE
598	  latents — so vision reaches the transformer *only* through what the text
599	  tokens absorbed from them. The tower conditions the text; the VAE
600	  conditions the pixels.
601	  **Q8.1 — the vision tower on CPU. Done** (`qimage/vision`, ~600 lines):
602	  all 27 blocks against the dump at **rel ≤ 1.1e-4**, the three deepstack
603	  features at ≤9.5e-5, the merged rows at 8.9e-5, and patchify / position
604	  grid / rope table exact to fp32 rounding (1e-7–5e-6). Four things here are
605	  not what a plain ViT does, and each is a **negative control that fires**:
606	  token order is 2x2-block-major rather than raster (raster is caught at
607	  **40717x** the bound); the block MLP's GELU is the tanh approximation
608	  while both mergers use the exact erf one (swapping them, **221x**); the
609	  rotation is NeoX halves and not the adjacent-pair convention
610	  `qimage/dit` uses one import away (**3796x**); and the output merger
611	  normalizes each 1152-wide row *before* concatenating four while the three
612	  deepstack mergers normalize the 4608-wide concatenation after — which the
613	  checkpoint's own norm widths refuse at load rather than answering wrongly.
614	  **Q8.2 — the edit text encoding on CPU. Done 2026-09-20**
615	  (`qimage/textenc/edit.go`, ~340 lines, plus one seam in `zimage/qwen`:
616	  `ForwardEmbeds` runs the layers over caller-supplied embeddings, a
617	  caller-supplied rotary table and a per-layer hook, and `Forward` is now
618	  that function with a token lookup and a plain 0..T-1 table in front of it —
619	  `embed`, `llm` and `parakeet` are untouched). Three mechanisms, each
620	  gated:
621	  - **the template**, with each image's `<|image_pad|>` expanded to one token
622	    per merged 2x2 group before tokenizing. `<image1>` is *not* a special
623	    token — it is four ordinary BPE ids — and the leading space before
624	    `<image2>` tokenizes, so both are rendered exactly.
625	  - **3-D positions**, transformers' `get_rope_index`: text runs advance all
626	    three axes off a shared counter, an image block lays its merged grid out
627	    in (t, h, w) raster order at the counter, and the counter then advances
628	    by the grid's **span**, `max(H, W)/merge` — 8 positions for a 64-token
629	    square image, 12 for a 72-token 192x384 one. Then the **interleaved**
630	    mrope table: frequency j reads h when j%3 == 1 and w when j%3 == 2 below
631	    3*section, t everywhere else.
632	  - **deepstack injection**: the merger's rows scatter into the pad slots
633	    before layer 0, and the three features are added at those slots after
634	    layers 0, 1 and 2. Several images are one stacked tensor in pad order,
635	    not a loop.
636	
637	  **Gates.** Without weights, exact: the ids, the pad slots and all three
638	  position axes for both the one- and two-image sequences, and the rotary
639	  tables at 2.7e-6 / 4.2e-6 against the ones the model built for itself.
640	  With weights, against the pipeline's own `prompt_embeds`: **one image —
641	  layer 0 at 1.4e-4, the pre-norm state 3.3e-4, `prompt_embeds` 4.3e-4**;
642	  **two images — the scattered `inputs_embeds` exactly (rel 0, max abs 0),
643	  layer 0 at 1.1e-5, the pre-norm state 4.1e-4, `prompt_embeds` 4.8e-4**,
644	  all against Q1's measured `deepTol` of 1e-3. Controls: plain RoPE instead
645	  of mrope **13315x** the bound, no deepstack injection **6057x**, and the
646	  conditions in the wrong order refused at the row count rather than
647	  answered.
648	
649	  **The dump grew a two-image case** — the 256² card plus a 192x384 one with
650	  a different pattern, 177 tokens and 136 slots — because one image hides
651	  the leading space, the span arithmetic and the cross-image stacking, and
652	  the endpoint promises ten. Two dump bugs came out of it, both in the
653	  reference rather than the port: the new section was missing the
654	  final-norm neutralization hook the single-image one installs (so its
655	  "prenorm" came back *normalized*, absmax 142 against `prompt_embeds`'
656	  661.9), and the fp32 tensors turned out not to be the right oracle for the
657	  wide card at all — see below.
658	
659	  **The method finding, a third time: measure the reference against itself.**
660	  The two-image gate first failed at rel 1.3e-2, with the worst element
661	  inside the second image's rows. Everything structural was already
662	  excluded — the pixel rows, the patch embedding and block 0 match to fp32
663	  rounding, and every geometric piece feeds them — and the error *grew with
664	  depth* (3.3e-5 at layer 8, 1.1e-4 at 16, 3.5e-4 at 24, 1.0e-3 at the last
665	  hidden state). Packing was not the cause: the reference is **bit-identical**
666	  running the two images batched or alone. What settled it was Q5's arbiter,
667	  the same tower in **float64**: the dumped **fp32 reference is itself rel
668	  8.9e-4 (last hidden) and 1.4e-3 (merged) from float64 on the wide card,
669	  against 1.0e-4 and 1.2e-4 on the square one** — the same code on a picture
670	  that amplifies rounding ten times harder. Against the float64 rows this
671	  port lands at **1.3e-4, 2.1e-4 and 4.8e-5, six to seven times closer than
672	  the fp32 reference**, because `qimage/vision` accumulates dot products in
673	  float64 while holding activations in float32. So the wide card's deep
674	  tower stages are gated against **dumped float64 rows at 5e-4**
675	  (`towerTol`), and the edit text encoding is gated with the *dump's own*
676	  condition rows, which is what makes it a gate on the text encoding rather
677	  than on the pair. The composed run — our tower feeding our encoder, which
678	  is what a served edit does — sits at **rel 1.3e-2 from a 1.6e-3 difference
679	  in the tower's merged rows**, reported with that attribution and guarded
680	  at an order of magnitude, not presented as a precision claim.
681	
682	  **Q8.3 — the edit pipeline on CPU. Done 2026-09-20**
683	  (`qimage/pipeline/edit.go`, `dit.LayoutFromPadMask`, and the oracle
684	  `reference/dump_qi21_edit.py` → `out/qi21edit`). The oracle is the t2i
685	  dump's deliberate twin — same size, same steps, same seed, noise passed in
686	  packed — with `output_resolution` set to the card's own size so the
687	  pipeline's condition resize is the *identity* and the gate is about the
688	  pipeline rather than a resampler. Two runs byte-identical over all 14
689	  tensors.
690	  Three pieces were new and each is small, because an edit reuses the t2i
691	  graph: **`LayoutFromPadMask`** turns the text encoder's own image-pad mask
692	  into the joint sequence's geometry (runs of true are the condition images,
693	  what is between them is text) and *generalises* `NewLayout` rather than
694	  sitting beside it — a t2i prompt has no slots and the two agree, which the
695	  test asserts so the edit path cannot become a second layout implementation;
696	  **`EncodeCondition`** runs the VAE encoder, takes the posterior mode,
697	  normalises per channel and packs; and **`CalcDimensions`**, diffusers'
698	  `calculate_dimensions`, whose rounding is Python's break-to-even and not
699	  away-from-zero.
700	  **The gate** (`TestEndToEndEdit`, the edit twin of `TestEndToEndImage`):
701	  condition image + prompt through our tokenizer, vision tower, text
702	  encoder, VAE encoder, DiT, scheduler and decoder, only the noise from the
703	  oracle — **prompt_embeds 4.7e-4, condition latents 6.5e-5, per-step
704	  latents 1.4e-4 → 4.4e-5, and the edited image at max abs 1.0e-5, mean
705	  2e-6** against the 2.2e-2 precedent. That is 90x tighter than the t2i
706	  gate's own image number, and the reason is the prefix: an edit's
707	  trajectory is pinned by 277 rows of conditioning where a generation's is
708	  free.
709	  **The finding, and it is a sharp one: the condition image must be
710	  quantized exactly like the reference's.** The vision copy is composited
711	  over white by PIL, which works on **uint8**, so every composited pixel
712	  lands on a level. Doing that arithmetic in float instead leaves 97% of the
713	  pixels half a level away — and the tower turns that into **rel 3.49 on the
714	  merged rows and rel 11.1 on the prompt embedding**, which is how this port
715	  first failed. It is now the stage's negative control, firing at 11115x the
716	  bound. Read together with the float64 measurement above, the tower
717	  amplifies an input perturbation by roughly **10³**, and the consequence is
718	  a requirement on the resampler, which is why it is ported exactly rather
719	  than approximately (below). None of this means an edit is fragile — a
720	  differently-quantized condition gives a different *valid* edit, the same
721	  way cache-on and cache-off do — but it does mean parity is only measurable
722	  against the same pixels.
723	
724	  **Q8.3b — the resampler. Done 2026-09-20** (`qimage/pipeline/resize.go`,
725	  ~200 lines). It is **Lanczos, not bicubic**: `VaeImageProcessor`'s default
726	  `resample` is `lanczos` and the pipeline constructs it without overriding
727	  that, so every condition image is resized by
728	  `PIL.Image.resize(resample=LANCZOS)`. The port reproduces Pillow's
729	  arithmetic rather than its intent — 22-bit fixed-point coefficients with
730	  its away-from-zero rounding, an int32 accumulator with its rounding term,
731	  its clip-and-shift, two passes with a **uint8 intermediate**, and its skip
732	  of a pass whose axis does not change — and the gate is **exact 8-bit
733	  equality**, not a tolerance, because at 10³ amplification "close" is not a
734	  claim worth making.
735	  Two things had to be got right that reading the filter would not tell you.
736	  The filter is stretched by the **downscale** factor only, so downscaling
737	  antialiases and upscaling does not; and **an RGBA image is not resampled
738	  as four independent channels** — `Image.resize` converts it to `RGBa`
739	  (premultiplied), resamples, and converts back, both conversions 8-bit and
740	  lossy. Missing the premultiply left 28% of samples up to four levels out,
741	  which is how the port first failed. It now matches on all three
742	  behaviours: **500x333 → 320x224 (down), 128x96 → 288x224 (up), and

# IMAGE — the Qwen-Image-2.1 vertical

> **Rewritten through 2026-09-20 — Q0–Q8 are done, the vertical's last
> capability is served, and Q9's first pass has been taken**: `POST
> /v1/images/generations` answers at **1m32s for a 1024²/40-step image** and
> `POST /v1/images/edits` at **1m59s for a 1024² edit on one reference**,
> 31.5 and 39.4 GB resident, reproducing the reference edit at **max abs
> 0.0014** — 24x tighter than the t2i path's own served number, because an
> edit's trajectory is pinned by its prefix. Q9 so far: a 6–7% step, bit for
> bit the same picture, from one badly-shaped launch the profile caught.
>
> **2026-09-21 — Q10: the ceiling is an area, not a box.** A served 16:9
> request was coming back 1024x576 against arenas that hold 1.05 Mpx, because
> the geometry limited each *side*. The VAE's arena turns out to be **exactly
> 3060 bytes a pixel for every aspect ratio** (`TestArenaShape`), so the shape
> was never a constraint: the same server now answers **1344x768**, 1.75x the
> pixels, at the same wall clock, and `-image-size 1184x1184` reaches
> **1536x864**. Nothing about residency or the numerics moved.
>
> **2026-09-21 — Q11: a hung-up client now stops the run.** The context
> reaches the sampler and the VAE's submit loop, so an abandoned request costs
> **one step (21% of a short run) or 295 ms of a decode** instead of the whole
> picture — and stops holding the process-wide device lock against every other
> vertical. The run after a cancellation is bit-identical to one before it.
>
> **Q0–Q7, one day in** and
> the model was *served*: `POST /v1/images/generations` answered from
> Qwen-Image-2.1 at **1m38s for a 1024²/40-step image** (Q6's own
> measurement; Q9 has since taken it to 1m32), 31.7 GB resident,
> with native RGBA and in-progress previews. On the CPU the port reproduces
> diffusers' image to under a quarter of an 8-bit quantization step; on the
> device the served fp16 path reproduces the fp32 oracle's own picture at
> **mean 3.4e-4**. What remains for the vertical is percents (Q9) — plus
> finishing the Z-Image deletion, which Q6 owes and half did.
> This file is live again: the old root
> `IMAGE.md` was frozen into
> [`research/zimage-vertical.md`](research/zimage-vertical.md) at the 2026-09-20
> consolidation, and this one is the **replacement of Z-Image-Turbo by
> `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`** for both generation and edits. Same rules as every
> vertical file: rewritten each session, not appended to; closed stages go to
> `research/`. Stage letters here are **Q0, Q1, …** (I-stages stay z-image's,
> in the archive).
>
> Breaking the current vertical while we do this was accepted up front
> (2026-09-20 session). Z-Image code gets deleted, not kept in parallel —
> except `zimage/qwen`, which `embed`, `llm` and `parakeet` also import
> (see "what survives").

**Target**: `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` — prompt → PNG (optionally RGBA) at up to
2048x2048, and native reference-image editing (up to 10 refs), end to end in
Go on Vulkan, served at `POST /v1/images/generations` and
`POST /v1/images/edits`, with in-progress previews.

## Where the work stands

| # | Stage | State |
|---|---|---|
| Q0 | Reference env + dumps (six oracles, `reference/dump_qi21_*.py`) | **done 2026-09-20** — incl. the saved 1024²/40 fp32 run; two runs byte-identical |
| Q1 | Text encoding in Go (`qimage/textenc` over an unchanged `zimage/qwen`) | **done** — CPU ≤7.1e-4 (its own noise floor measured), GPU fp16 characterized 10-85x tighter than the official bf16 |
| Q2 | One DiT block on CPU (`qimage/dit`) | **done** — block, cache contents, both regimes ≤4e-5; negative control 1e5x |
| Q3 | Stack + scheduler + sampler on CPU (`qimage/pipeline`) | **done** — per-step latents 2.1e-5→2.5e-4 vs the oracle |
| Q5 | VAE on CPU (`qimage/vae`) + the end-to-end image gate | **done** — decoder/encoder stagewise; **prompt→image matches diffusers at max abs 9.1e-4** (24x inside the 2.2e-2 precedent) |
| Q4 | DiT on the GPU (`qimage/dit/gpu.go`) | **done for t2i** — teacher-forced flat ≤8e-3 over 40 steps; **2.27 s/step at 1024²** |
| Q5g | VAE decoder on the GPU (`qimage/vae/gpu.go`) | **done 2026-09-20** — stagewise on the dump's own bounds; **1024² in 7.4 s**, 117 dispatches. Encoder stays CPU until Q8 needs it |
| Q6 | Serve t2i (`/v1/images/generations`, RGBA, ceiling geometry) | **done 2026-09-20** — `qimage/pipeline` resident at **31.7 GB**, served 1024²/40 in **1m38.2s / 1m41.3s**, `background: "transparent"` answered; Z-Image deletion still owed |
| Q7 | Previews (fitted linear 64→RGB; no tiny AE exists for this VAE) | **done 2026-09-20** — R² 0.97, **159 µs a frame**, three partials cost 0.3% of a request; previews are unconditional, the flags are gone |
| Q8 | Edits (vision tower, multi-ref, VAE encoder serving) | **done 2026-09-20** — `/v1/images/edits` answers from a **2m8s served edit at 1024²**, 39.4 GB resident, reproducing the reference edit at **max abs 0.0014, mean 1.7e-4** (24x tighter than t2i's own served number); seventeen controls firing |

## The model, as the checkpoint describes it

Three components, ~32.3 GB on disk (bf16), against Z-Image's ~20 GB resident:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| DiT | `QwenImage21Transformer2DModel` — **32 single-stream blocks**, dim 4096 (32 heads x 128), SwiGLU **12288** (mlp_ratio 3), **no biases anywhere**, per-head-dim q/k RMSNorm (eps 1e-6), 7.1 B params | 14 GB |
| Text encoder | **Qwen3-VL-8B** (`Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`): text model 36 layers, hidden 4096, 32 q / 8 kv heads of 128, theta **5e6**, vocab 151936; plus a 27-layer vision tower (hidden 1152, patch 16, spatial-merge 2, deepstack taps at layers 8/16/24) | 17 GB |
| VAE | `AutoencoderKLQwenImage21` — Wan-lineage causal-3D residual conv AE, encoder base 96 / decoder base **144**, dim_mult [1,2,4,8,8], **z_dim 64, 16x spatial**, **4-channel RGBA in and out**, per-channel `latents_mean/std` (64 values each) | 1.3 GB |

Geometry: **one latent token = one 16x16 pixel tile** (patch_size 1, VAE /16).
Pixel sides must be multiples of **32** (the VLM groups latent tokens 2x2).
1024² = 4096 image tokens — the same DiT sequence length as Z-Image at 1024².
2048² (the model's native size) = 16384. Defaults: **40 steps, no CFG**
(`true_cfg_scale=1.0`; true-CFG exists but is off by design), pipeline default
resolution **1024²** (the README's examples use 2048² explicitly).

### The four mechanisms that make it different from Z-Image

**1. One joint sequence, block-causal.** Text embeddings and image latents
share a single stream. The mask is `(q_idx >= kv_idx) OR same_image_block`:
the sequence is causal, text tokens strictly so, but every image block (each
condition image, and the target) is internally bidirectional. In diffusers the
non-flex processor decomposes this exactly into one attention call per prefix
segment (text segments get a causal triangle) plus one full-attention call for
the target — that decomposition, not a masked kernel, is the shape we port.

**2. `causal_condition` + prefix KV cache.** Text and condition-image tokens
are modulated from **t = 0** (the modulation tensor carries batch+1 rows; the
target's tokens read their sample's row, everything else reads the t=0 row).
That makes the prefix's activations step-independent, so **step 0 runs the
full block-causal prefill and stores per-layer post-RoPE K/V for the prefix;
steps 1..N-1 recompute only the target's tokens**, attending over
[cached prefix K/V ++ fresh target K/V] with no mask at all (batch 1, no
padding). For t2i the prefix is just the prompt (tens of tokens — small win);
for edits it is thousands of tokens per reference image (large win). Caching
on/off changes rounding, not correctness — diffusers documents that the two
settings give *visibly different but equally valid* samples. **We ship
cache-on and validate against diffusers `use_kv_cache=True`.**

**3. Sequence assembly and RoPE.** The VLM sequence's `<|image_pad|>` slots
each stand for a **2x2 group of latent tokens**: the transformer expands those
positions four-fold and drops VAE latents into them; the target's slots are
appended after the text. Text embeddings pass through `txt_in` (zero-centered
RMSNorm → 4096→4096 → GELU-tanh → 4096→4096); latents through `img_in`
(64→4096, no bias). RoPE is 3-axis (frame/h/w, dims 16/56/56, theta 10000),
complex adjacent-pair rotation — **the same pairing as Z-Image's DiT**, not
the NeoX halves of the text encoder. Text advances all three axes together;
each image block freezes the frame axis and lays h/w out on a **zero-centered
grid with negative indices** (a flipped negative-frequency table serves
indices −1024..−1); after an image block the position cursor advances by
`max(h, w)`.

**4. Shared modulation.** One `SiLU → Linear(4096→16384)` for the whole
model — blocks own no adaLN parameters. Each block chunks it into
(scale1, gate1, scale2, gate2); gates pass through **tanh**; norms are plain
non-affine LayerNorm. Final head: scale-only AdaLN + `proj_out` 4096→64.
Timestep embedding: sinusoidal 256 (cos first half — Z-Image convention
differs, check the dump), then a bias-free MLP to 4096.

### Text encoding, exactly

Raw template strings, **not** `apply_chat_template` (the two tokenize
differently and the checkpoint expects the raw form):

```
t2i:  <|im_start|>system\nComprehend and analyze the provided prompt.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\n{prompt}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n
edit: same, with "<image1><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>" (then " <image2>…" etc.) prefixed to the user text
```

- The embedding is the **last decoder layer's output *before* the final
  RMSNorm** (all 36 layers run — different from Z-Image's `hidden_states[-2]`
  where the last layer never ran). transformers 5.x silently normalizes
  `hidden_states[-1]`; diffusers neutralizes that with a forward hook on the
  final norm, and Q0 **verified the hook on transformers 5.17.0**: the hooked
  `hidden_states[-1]` equals the pipeline's output exactly (gap 0), so 5.17
  is the dump env — the model card requires >= 5.17 anyway.
- Drop the first `drop_idx` tokens, where drop_idx = length of the tokenized
  system message (computed, not hardcoded). Empty prompt becomes `" "`.
- For edits, condition images additionally go through the vision tower (RGBA
  flattened over white **for the vision copy only**); mrope with real 3D
  positions at image slots. Text-only prompts make mrope collapse to standard
  NeoX RoPE — **verified in Q0**: the model's own cos/sin tables for a text
  prompt match a plain theta-5e6 table to 0.0 (`mrope_gap` in the textenc
  manifest), so nothing mrope-shaped is needed before Q8.
- A fact Q8 rests on, confirmed while building the head dump: **the VLM's
  image-slot embedding rows are overwritten by the VAE latents** in the joint
  stream. Vision content reaches the DiT only through what the *text* tokens
  absorbed from the image inside the text encoder's own attention. The vision
  tower conditions the text; the VAE conditions the pixels.

### Scheduler

FlowMatchEulerDiscrete with **dynamic shifting**: sigmas `linspace(1, 1/N, N)`,
`mu` linear in the **target** token count between (256, 0.5) and (8192, 0.9)
— at 1024², mu = 0.6935, and **unclamped past 8192**: 2048² extrapolates to
mu = 1.3129 (measured, Q0) — `time_shift_type: exponential`,
`shift_terminal: 0.02`, `stochastic_sampling: false`. Port from diffusers'
scheduler, not from Z-Image's fixed shift 3.0. The scheduler steps **only the
target latents** (the model's output rows for the prefix are discarded).
VAE decode applies `z * std + mean` per channel; encode the inverse, and uses
the **posterior mode** (`argmax`), which keeps our seed-reproducibility rule
for free.

## What this changes about the vertical (semantics, not code)

- **Edits stop being SDEdit.** Today an edit is a truncated generation
  (strength ⇒ steps skipped ⇒ cheaper). In 2.1 an edit is a *conditional
  generation*: reference latents + vision context as prefix, target from pure
  noise, all 40 steps. An edit becomes **slightly more expensive** than a
  generation (bigger prefix), the `strength` knob disappears, and up to **10
  reference images** arrive (OpenAI's `image[]` array already allows several).
  `/v1/images/edits` keeps its shape; its documentation changes meaning.
  **Measured, Q8.6**: 2m8s against a generation's 1m38s at 1024² with one
  reference, `strength` is a 400 explaining the change, and how many
  references a given server takes is `-edits N` and `max_reference_images`.
- **RGBA is native.** The VAE emits 4 channels always; transparency is asked
  for in the prompt (the model card's recommended phrasing). Map OpenAI's
  `background: "transparent"` to that prompt prefix + PNG-with-alpha out;
  opaque requests composite over white.
- **Masked / annotated local edits** (circles, painted regions, separate
  masks) are a *capability the model has* — the current 501 for masks may
  become closable. How a separate mask is fed (extra condition image?) is not
  in the diffusers PR; needs the examples repo before promising it (open
  question Q-o3).
- **The cost profile inverts — now measured, no longer estimated.**
  Z-Image-Turbo was an 8-step distillation at 14.3 s an image; 2.1 wants 40
  steps, and Q4's GPU DiT measures **2.27 s a cached step, 2.29 s the
  prefill: 90.7 s of transformer per 1024² image** (the morning's estimate
  said ~70 s; the gap is unported fusions and the full-seq re-pack, priced
  under Q9). **Q6 measured the whole thing served: 1m38.2s / 1m41.3s at
  1024²/40** — 92% the denoising steps, 7.6% the VAE, 0.1% the text encoder.
  Q9's two priced VAE ports would take the decode from 7.5 s to ~1.3 s, i.e.
  the image to ~92 s; everything past that is the DiT's.
  2048² is not reachable at all today — the VAE's arena ceiling is 1184²
  (Q6) — so the DiT's x4/x16 estimate for it is moot until that is lifted.
  The two levers, in order: **the step count** (sweep 40/24/16/12 for
  quality — the knob exists, and at 2.27 s/step it is the difference between
  ~90 s and ~27 s) and **a distilled/turbo release or LoRA** (the ecosystem
  — lightx2v etc. — is where Z-Image-Turbo itself came from; watch for it).
  **Q6's sweep decides the served default**; 1024²/40 is the starting point,
  not a commitment.

## The preview problem (taef1 has no successor here)

`madebyollin/taehv`'s **taew2_1 does *not* fit this model**: it decodes the
Wan-2.1 16-channel/8x latent that the *original* Qwen-Image borrowed; 2.1's
VAE is a new 64-channel/16x RGBA design, and as of today taehv lists nothing
for it. So, in order:

1. **Q7 shipped a fitted linear preview** (done 2026-09-20): a 64→4 matrix,
   least-squares over (latent, 1/16-scale image) pairs — the latent2rgb
   approach. One GEMV per latent pixel, measured at 159 µs a frame; a 1024²
   generation previews at 64x64, upscaled client-side. The fitting data is
   *generated* rather than taken from Q0's dumps (`cmd/previewfit`, 24
   prompts spanning colour and content), because a pair the pipeline
   produced itself cannot disagree with it about normalisation or layout.
2. **Watch taehv** for a 2.1 variant and port it like `zimage/vae/tiny.go`
   (at T=1 its temporal machinery degenerates; it would be a small 2D conv
   stack again). Do not build our own distilled decoder — that is a training
   project this repo does not want.

## The stages

Same doctrine as every vertical: **CPU reference first, validated against a
dump, then the GPU port debugged against the CPU one.** One stage, one gate,
two-run numbers.

- **Q0 — reference environment and dumps. Done 2026-09-20**, full-size
  oracle included: `out/qi21run1024` is the saved 1024²/40 fp32 CPU run
  (~52 s/step, ~35 min, ~68 GB — nothing else heavy may run beside it; a
  34 GB Go test alongside got both OOM-killed), and its PNG is a
  photorealistic render of the prompt. The env: the shared `.venv` with torch
  2.14.0+cpu, transformers 5.17.0, torchvision 0.29.0+cpu, accelerate, and
  **diffusers 0.41.0.dev0 pinned to git commit `80c7ed26`** (stable 0.40.0
  predates the merge); `reference/qwenimage21/` is byte-identical to the
  installed package. Five scripts, all fp32 CPU, all in `reference/`:
  - `dump_qi21_sched.py` → `out/qi21sched` — sigma/timestep tables for five
    size/step cases plus one Euler step over deterministic vectors.
  - `dump_qi21_dit.py` → `out/qi21dit` — everything around the blocks
    (num_layers=0, 9 tensors): txt_in/img_in, joint assembly, RoPE tables,
    image_ids/target mask, the t=0 modulation row, prefill and cached
    forwards, for a t2i case and a synthetic edit case. The
    prefill-vs-cached identity at 0 blocks measured exactly 0.
  - `dump_qi21_dit_block.py` → `out/qi21block` — block 0 with real weights
    in prefill/extract/cached modes, cache K/V contents included; the fp32
    cached-vs-prefill gap on target rows measured **≤ 3.8e-6** (t2i), 0
    (edit) — Q4's numeric bound.
  - `dump_qi21_vae.py` → `out/qi21vae` — decode from seeded noise and encode
    of a deterministic RGBA test card (posterior **mode**), per-child and
    per-up/down-block intermediates hooked, 256² and 192x320. Decode clamps
    to [-1,1]; encoder conv_out is 128 = 64 mean + 64 logvar.
  - `dump_qi21_run.py` → `out/qi21run` + `out/qi21run2` — the end-to-end
    oracle: 256²/4 steps, seed 42, kv-cache on, noise passed in packed (the
    Go side gets it as data, not torch RNG), per-step latents, final RGBA
    image + PNG. **Two runs byte-identical**, and the PNG is recognizably
    the prompt. `--size 1024 --steps 40 --out out/qi21run1024` is the saved
    full-size run.
  - `dump_qi21_textenc.py` → `out/qi21textenc` — runs the pipeline's own
    `_get_qwen_prompt_embeds` (en / cjk / empty prompts), plus a layer walk
    (embed, layers 0-1, last-prenorm) and the rope cos/sin capture that
    settled Q-o5. drop_idx = 14 for the shipped system prompt.
- **Q1 — text encoding in Go. Done 2026-09-20.** `zimage/qwen` needed **no
  change at all** — `qimage/textenc` (the tree's first package) supplies the
  nested-`text_config` adapter (Prefix `model.language_model.`), the raw t2i
  template, the tokenized-system-message drop, and `Drop`; `Load(dir,
  cfg.NumLayers)` already expresses "all 36 layers, no final norm". Gates:
  tokenizer exact on en/cjk/empty; layer walk ≤ 2e-5; **CPU encoder en
  1.6e-4 / cjk 8.6e-5 / empty 7.1e-4 against a `deepTol` of 1e-3** — measured,
  not chosen: the reference disagrees with *itself* by 3.2e-4 on the empty
  prompt when only the attention kernel changes (eager vs sdpa), so
  z-image's 2e-4 sits below this model's own fp32 noise floor at depth 36.
  **GPU encoder (fp16, unchanged kernels) en/cjk 0.024-0.027, empty 0.21**,
  and that number has a mechanism (`TestGPULadder`, kept as the permanent
  instrument): the residual stream grows a ~13k massive-activation channel
  at layer 6, carries it flat, and **cancels it in layers 34-35 — the two
  layers Z-Image never ran** — so the fp16 bulk-rounding variance the
  channel accumulated surfaces at the end (protecting just the spike
  elements measurably does not help). Priced against deployment: the
  **official bf16 pipeline deviates from fp32 by rel 2.0 (abs 204)** through
  the same mechanism — our fp16 path is 10-85x closer to fp32 than what the
  ecosystem ships. Not taken (priced): an fp32-activation GEMM arm for the
  encoder — at prompt-sized M (~40 rows) the encoder is weight-bandwidth-
  bound so it would be cheap; build it only if Q3/Q6 show prompt adherence
  suffering.
- **Q2 — one DiT block on CPU. Done 2026-09-20** (`qimage/dit`): layout
  (image ids/target mask/segments) **exact** vs the dump, RoPE tables at
  ~5e-7 (negative-index grids included), head pieces at ~1e-5, the no-block
  prefill/cached forwards at ~4e-6, and the block gate — out_prefill,
  cache K/V contents, out_cached, both cases — at **≤ 4e-5** against
  `out/qi21block`. The negative control (NeoX-halves rotary pairing) is
  caught at 1e5x the bound. `Load(dir, blocks)` takes 0/1/32 blocks, so Q3's
  stack is a loop away. One porting trap found and worth remembering:
  `chunk(2, -1)` splits *rows* — rewrapping the modulation's backing array
  at half width hands row 1 the second half of row 0, and every downstream
  tensor fails at rel ~10 while every shape checks out.
- **Q3 — the stack + scheduler + t2i sampler on CPU. Done 2026-09-20 at the
  latent gate** (`qimage/pipeline`): the dynamic-shift scheduler matches
  diffusers at ~1e-6 across all five dumped size/step cases (mu exact, the
  exponential shift, the terminal stretch, the Euler step), and
  `Denoise` — 32 blocks, ModeExtract at step 0 then cached decodes, exactly
  as served — reproduces the 256²/4-step oracle's **per-step latents at
  rel 2.1e-5 → 2.5e-4** (bound 1e-3, 4x measured; 2.3 min a sample on CPU).
  **Still owed to Q5**: the *image* gate — prompt → PNG with our own text
  encoder and VAE decode against the oracle's `image` tensor (Z-Image's
  2.2e-2 precedent). The three green gates (textenc, denoise, decoder) do
  not compose into that claim; it gets measured, once the decoder exists.
- **Q4 — DiT on the GPU. Done 2026-09-20 for t2i** (`qimage/dit/gpu.go`,
  ~750 lines on z-image's shader set): **1024²/40 steps in 90.7 s — prefill
  2.29 s, cached steps 2.27 s** — against CPU Go's ~2.5 h and torch fp32's
  ~35 min. The mapping that made it small: the block's LayerNorm+modulate+
  narrow is `dit_final_norm.comp` verbatim; the shared modulation is host
  arithmetic (ten uploaded vectors) with the t=0 row-select expressed as two
  dispatch ranges; SwiGLU's fp16 range problem is solved *exactly* by
  scaling 1/16 into fp16 and folding 16 into the uploaded tanh(gate) vector
  (2.1's down-proj feeds a gated residual, so z-image's norm-invariance
  trick was unavailable). Two new shaders: `dit_attn_causal.comp` (the
  prefill runs the WMMA kernel bidirectionally over the whole sequence and
  this recomputes the text rows' context causally — tens of rows, once per
  image) and `dit_copy.comp` (offset copies for the KV cache). The cache is
  each block's post-RoPE prefix k/v as fp32 arena rows, restored under the
  fresh target rows each step before a full re-pack (fine at t2i's tiny
  prefix; Q8's reference images want it fp16 + tile-masked, and the
  full-seq re-pack is a Q9 percent). **Gates, per
  `two-row-regime-needs-a-graph-gate`, both regimes against the oracle**:
  teacher-forced (each step fed the oracle's own latents — bounds the
  model) flat at 1.5e-3–8e-3 over all 40 steps at 1024², bound 2e-2;
  free-running drifts linearly at ~1.3e-3/step to 0.050 at 40 steps — a
  perturbed ODE diverging, the phenomenon diffusers documents for
  cache-on/off — bounded at 0.12 with the image judgment deferred to Q6's
  eyeball. Not done: tile re-screen at M=16384/K=12288 (running on
  z-image's measured winners uncontested — a Q9 percent), the VAE's GPU
  stage (with Q5's fp16-range constraint), and the negative-control
  breakages the z-image graph carries.
- **Q5 — the VAE in Go. CPU done 2026-09-20** (`qimage/vae`, on
  `zimage/vae`'s Tensor/Conv2D — whose Pad/PadEnd/Stride already carried the
  identical downsampler shape): decoder and encoder, stagewise against
  `out/qi21vae`, RGBA round trip included. The T=1 semantics are explicit in
  the package doc: causal 3D convs fold to 2D, time_convs never run,
  AvgDown3D *means in a zero frame* on temporal blocks, DupUp3D keeps only
  the last temporal copy. Two measured bounds: conv stages at 2e-4 (they run
  at ≤5e-5), and `normTol` 8e-3 for the stages where the model amplifies
  fp32 noise — the decoder past its per-pixel L2 tail norm (the dumped fp32
  reference is itself rel 1.3e-3 from a float64 decode there; our decoded
  image sits max abs 8.7e-4 from the dump, under a quarter of one 8-bit
  step) and the encoder's deep middle (the reference's own thread-order
  noise jumps 47x at down_blocks.3; we track ~5x that and land at 4.7e-5 on
  the posterior mode).
  **The end-to-end image gate Q3 owed is closed**: `TestEndToEndImage` runs

861	  (`qimage/dit/gpu.go`, ~120 lines changed; `dit_kvcache.comp` and a rewrite

868	  Four things had to change, and three of them are about the prefix being
869	  thousands of rows instead of forty:
870	  - **The condition latents go through `img_in`.** They are latents in the
871	    same sequence, so they take the target's own projection — one GEMM per
872	    condition block off the same narrowed `aLat`, issued in ascending row
873	    order because a GEMM writes whole 128-row tiles and overruns a short
874	    block. The projected *text* rows then land by copy dispatch rather than
875	    by host write, since a host write cannot be ordered after a dispatch
876	    that has not been submitted.
877	  - **The block-causal mask is repaired segment by segment, last segment
878	    first.** Every row attends to a contiguous key prefix — its own index
879	    for a text token, its image block's last index for an image token — so
880	    the matrix-core pass still runs bidirectionally over the whole sequence
881	    (right for the target) and each prefix segment is then recomputed with
882	    its own key count. Backwards, because the WMMA kernel's query block
883	    starts at row 0 and an image segment's pass necessarily rewrites every
884	    row before it; running in reverse makes each row's last writer its own
885	    segment. It costs about a quarter again of the prefill's attention and
886	    needs no new matrix-core kernel.

888	    with a query-row offset and an optional fixed key count. That lifts the
889	    512-key cap it carried (a text run in the middle of an edit's prefix
890	    attends over the condition image before it) and costs nothing at t2i:
891	    for a prefix inside one chunk the arithmetic order is unchanged, and
892	    `TestGPUOracle256` comes back **bit-identical** (0.001503 / 0.00148
893	    before and after).

895	    (`dit_kvcache.comp`). 32 blocks x 2 x 4136 rows x 4096 is **4.34 GB of
896	    fp32**, past this device's 4 GiB single-buffer cap; as halves it is
897	    **2.07 GB**, measured. The narrowing is *free*, not a trade: the pack
898	    narrows those rows to halves before attention reads them either way, so
899	    storing `fp32(fp16(x))` and packing it gives the same half.

1127	  0.5%) broken toward the closer ratio. That is what picks 1344x768 at 1.05
1128	  Mpx and the *exact* 1536x864 at 1.40, where a plain "largest that fits"
1129	  would have taken 1568x864 and been 2% wider than asked.
1130	  Two things deliberately did not change: the hard limit is still the VAE's
1131	  single storage buffer (now stated as **1,403,584 pixels** rather than
1132	  1184x1184, which is the same number said correctly), and `-image-size` is
1133	  still one flag naming both the default size and the ceiling — its *area* is
1134	  now what the ceiling means.
1135	- **Q11 — a hung-up client stops the run. Done 2026-09-21.** The context now
1136	  reaches the sampler, the VAE's submit loop, the vision tower and the VAE
1137	  encoder, instead of being checked once on the way into `backend.Image`.
1138	  **The granularity argument was half right and that is what made it worth
1139	  fixing.** A denoising step *is* a submit-and-fence with nothing to abandon
1140	  inside it — that much was true and is why no kernel changed here — but
1141	  between two steps nothing is in flight, and the VAE already batches its
1142	  dispatches four at a time for the driver's watchdog, which is 30 more
1143	  boundaries in a 1024² decode. So the finest available granularity was never
1144	  "the whole image"; it was one step and one batch, and nobody had gone and
1145	  taken it.
1146	  **Measured** (`TestCancellation`, the gate, at 512²/8 where a full run is
1147	  6.27 s): cancelled after step 1, the run returns in **1.30 s — 21% of the
1148	  full run** — with `pipeline: cancelled at step 2 of 8: context canceled`;
1149	  cancelled an eighth of the way into a 1.71 s decode, it returns in
1150	  **295 ms, after 12 of 117 dispatches**. At the served 1024²/40 shape that
1151	  is ~2.2 s of a 92 s image instead of 92.
1152	  **The third assertion is the one that would have hurt**: a cancelled run
1153	  leaves a recorded graph half-submitted and the arenas holding an abandoned
1154	  image, so the gate runs a *fourth* generation after the two cancellations
1155	  and requires it **bit-identical** to the one before them. It is. Nothing
1156	  about the device state survives a cancel, because nothing is left in
1157	  flight to survive it — which is the same property that made the step
1158	  boundary safe in the first place.
1159	  **What this is really worth is the lock.** `backend.Device` is one mutex
1160	  for every vertical in the process (one queue, nothing in `vk` externally
1161	  synchronised), and it is held for the whole run — so an abandoned image
1162	  was holding every queued speech, transcription and embedding request
1163	  behind it for its full duration, not merely wasting its own GPU time.
1164	  Text completions have always cancelled between tokens; **speech and
1165	  transcription still check only on the way in**, and are the same shape of
1166	  fix if an utterance ever gets long enough to care.
1167	  One thing came free with it: `cmd/qimage` takes its context from
1168	  `signal.NotifyContext`, so Ctrl-C now unwinds a run through the same path a
1169	  hung-up client takes rather than killing the process mid-submit.
1170	
1171	## Decisions taken now (so future sessions don't relitigate)
1172	
1173	1. **New `qimage/` tree; `zimage/qwen` and `zimage/tokenizer` stay put** until
1174	   z-image is fully gone, then a mechanical rename can hoist them.
1175	2. **KV cache always on** — validate against diffusers `use_kv_cache=True`;
1176	   cache-off exists only as a debug path if Q4 needs it.
1177	3. **Posterior mode (argmax) for every VAE encode** — matches the reference
1178	   and our reproducibility rule.
1179	4. **1024² default, 2048² behind the ceiling flag**, pending Q6's numbers —
1180	   amended 2026-09-20: 2048² is not a flag away. The decoder's arena stops
1181	   at **1184²** on one storage buffer (Q5g), so serving above that needs
1182	   tiling or a multi-buffer arena first. 1024² is the shipped default and
1183	   `-image-size` refuses anything larger than 1184x1184 at startup.
1184	   Amended again 2026-09-21 (Q10): **the ceiling is that rectangle's area and
1185	   not its sides** — 1,403,584 pixels, whatever shape they are in — because
1186	   the arena is 3060 bytes a pixel for every aspect ratio and a side limit
1187	   was charging landscape requests for a constraint that does not exist.
1188	5. **No self-trained tiny decoder**; linear preview + watch taehv.
1189	6. **No CFG path in the Go port** (true_cfg_scale stays a refusal if asked
1190	   for over HTTP) until something demands it — it would double every step.
1191	
1192	## Open questions
1193	
1194	- ~~**Q-o1**: how far below 40 steps does quality hold?~~ **Settled
1195	  2026-09-20 (Q6 sweep)**: it depends on the prompt, which is why the
1196	  default stays 40. Photographic and painterly prompts hold to **12 steps**
1197	  (36 s); a structured technical drawing is fine at 24 and broken at 12. The
1198	  headline is therefore **~1m38s at the safe default**, with 24 steps at
1199	  1m4s available to any client that sends `steps`.
1200	- **Q-o2**: does a turbo/distilled 2.1 checkpoint or step-distillation LoRA
1201	  appear? (Watch the examples repo and lightx2v.)
1202	- **Q-o3**: how are separate masks / painted annotations fed for local edits?
1203	  (Examples repo, before `/v1/images/edits` promises masks.)
1204	- **Q-o4**: does taehv grow a 2.1 variant? (Q7 fallback becomes an upgrade.)
1205	- ~~**Q-o5**: text-only mrope — confirmed equivalent to plain RoPE by dump?~~
1206	  **Settled 2026-09-20 (Q0)**: gap 0.0 against a plain theta-5e6 NeoX table;
1207	  `zimage/qwen` needs nothing mrope-shaped before Q8.
