> **2026-09-21 — Q9b: the VAE's two priced ports, and the price was wrong.**
> The ledger below had them as z-image's matrix-core kernels reused, worth
> ~6 s of a 7.5 s decode. **The instrument it said to build first refused the
> whole route** (`TestConvFP16Ladder`): a single fp16 operand anywhere in this
> decoder moves the decoded image by **max abs 0.09** against the fp32 path's
> own 7.3e-4 — narrowing *one* convolution, `conv_in`, which is 0.006% of the
> arithmetic, costs 0.0885 by itself, because the tail norm divides a
> per-pixel L2 out of a residual stream running at absmax 2.6e5. So the
> arithmetic stayed fp32 and only the *shape* changed — a register block the
> conv kernel had carried since the day 8 beat 1, and a 64x64 tiled fp32 GEMM
> for four projections that had been re-reading a whole weight per row. The
> decode goes **7.4 s → 4.02/4.03 s**, the VAE encoder **1.7 s → 0.91 s**, the
> served image **1m32 → 1m28.8/1m29.8** and the served edit **1m59 →
> 1m54.2/1m56.6** — and **every output is bit-identical**, asserted rather
> than assumed, so not one gate in this file moved a digit.
>

Everything else in the decode is under 4%: attention 250 ms (the latent is
  4096 rows here, not z-image's 16384 — this is *not* the 26% it was there),
  chnorm 1.7% with its SiLU already fused, add 1.0%, the two shuffles 0.4%.

  **What that port has to price first, and it is not in z-image's notes.**
  Every percent taken on 2026-09-20 was **bit-identical** — a launch shape
  and a kernel choice, no arithmetic moved. The conv port is not: the
  matrix-core convolution narrows its *operands* to fp16, and this decoder's
  convolutions read activations at **absmax 1.1e4** where z-image's peaked
  at **497**. Both are inside half's 65504, so neither overflows and the
  measurement that matters is not range but precision: an fp16 operand
  carries ~5e-4 of relative error, and `vae_test.go`'s conv stages are gated
  at **2e-4** with the decoded image at max abs 7.3e-4 against the dump.
  So the port moves the numbers this vertical's tightest gates are written
  against, and the first thing it owes is the same instrument every other
  bound here came from — run the CPU decoder with fp16 conv operands and
  fp32 accumulators, measure what it costs stagewise and on the image, and
  gate the device at *that* rather than at the fp32 bounds it will not hold.
  z-image made the same trade and kept its gates, but 20x less input range
  is 20x less headroom, and assuming it transfers is exactly the composition
  this file's method refuses. The infrastructure is otherwise ready:

- **Q9b — the VAE's two priced ports. Done 2026-09-21, and the price was
  wrong.** The ledger had them as z-image's matrix-core kernels reused —
  conv3x3 at 68.8% and 3.2 TFLOP/s against the 38.3 its implicit GEMM
  measured, the mid block's four projections at 21.0% and 35 GFLOP/s against
  the `dit_gemm` that replaced the same naive kernel there. **Both were
  refused on precision, and the same percents were taken in fp32 instead.**
  The decode goes **7.39–7.49 s → 4.02/4.03 s**, the VAE encoder
  **1.65–1.72 s → 0.909/0.915 s**, the served image **1m32.3/1m33.5 →
  1m28.8/1m29.8** and the served edit **1m58.6/1m59.2 → 1m54.2/1m56.6**.

  **The refusal came from the instrument the ledger itself said to build
  first, and it is the day's finding** (`TestConvFP16Ladder`, the permanent
  instrument: the CPU decoder and encoder run with chosen convolutions
  narrowing both operands to binary16 and accumulating in fp32 — what a
  matrix core does — against both the dump and the fp32 CPU port).
  The prediction in the ledger was "20x less headroom than z-image, measure
  it". The measurement is far worse than that framing suggests:

  | narrowed | decoded image, max abs | mean |
  |---|---|---|
  | nothing (the shipped fp32 device port) | 0.00073 | — |
  | `conv_in` alone — **one** convolution, 0.006% of the arithmetic | **0.0885** | 9.1e-5 |
  | the three learned upsamplers | 0.0948 | 9.2e-5 |
  | every 3x3 (what the port would narrow) | **0.178** | 2.0e-4 |
  | every convolution | **NaN** — up_blocks.4's shortcut reads absmax 2.6e5 |

  **It is not a range problem and no exclusion rule fixes it.** 0.178 in
  [-1, 1] is 23 of 255 8-bit levels, 240x the whole device port's distance
  from the dump; and one narrowed convolution at the very top of the graph
  costs half of that on its own, which is what says the damage is not
  located anywhere. **The mechanism is the tail norm.** This decoder's
  residual stream runs at absmax 1e4–2.6e5 and `norm_out` divides a
  per-pixel L2 out of it, so a 5e-4 *relative* perturbation upstream is an
  absolute 1e2 that a quiet pixel's own norm cannot absorb — measured at
  norm_out as **rel 1.13 against a mean of 6.7e-5**. And it is linear, not
  chaotic: the fp32 GPU path differs from the CPU one by rel ~1e-7 and lands
  4.9e-4 from it on the image, so a 5e-4 perturbation predicting ~0.2 is the
  same amplification read forwards. z-image's decoder peaks at **497** and
  has a group norm; the inheritance was never a small extrapolation.
  The **encoder** is worse again and would have been taken along silently:
  fp16 convolutions move its posterior mode by **max abs 0.23–0.40** against
  a port gated at 4.7e-5, through the deep middle the dump's own thread-order
  noise already jumps 47x at.

  **So the arithmetic stayed fp32 and only the shape changed** — which is
  where both kernels were actually losing, and the profile said so all along:

  - **the convolution is bound by activation loads**, one per `OC_BLOCK`
    multiply-adds, and `OC_BLOCK` had been 8 since the day it beat 1.
    `TestGPUKernelScreen` sweeps nine builds of `vae_conv2d.comp` over both
    blocking axes and the winner is **OC_BLOCK 48 / IC_BLOCK 8: 5.12 s →

said ~70 s; the gap is unported fusions and the full-seq re-pack, priced
  under Q9). **Q6 measured the whole thing served: 1m38.2s / 1m41.3s at
  1024²/40** — 92% the denoising steps, 7.6% the VAE, 0.1% the text encoder.
  Q9's two priced VAE ports would take the decode from 7.5 s to ~1.3 s, i.e.
  the image to ~92 s; everything past that is the DiT's.
  2048² is not reachable at all today — the VAE's arena ceiling is 1184²
  (Q6) — so the DiT's x4/x16 estimate for it is moot until that is lifted.
  "the whole image"; it was one step and one batch, and nobody had gone and
  taken it.
  **Measured** (`TestCancellation`, the gate, at 512²/8 where a full run is
  6.27 s): cancelled after step 1, the run returns in **1.30 s — 21% of the
  full run** — with `pipeline: cancelled at step 2 of 8: context canceled`;
  cancelled an eighth of the way into a 1.71 s decode, it returns in
  **295 ms, after 12 of 117 dispatches**. At the served 1024²/40 shape that
  is ~2.2 s of a 92 s image instead of 92.
  **The third assertion is the one that would have hurt**: a cancelled run
  leaves a recorded graph half-submitted and the arenas holding an abandoned
  image, so the gate runs a *fourth* generation after the two cancellations
  and requires it **bit-identical** to the one before them. It is. Nothing
  about the device state survives a cancel, because nothing is left in
  flight to survive it — which is the same property that made the step
  boundary safe in the first place.
  **What this is really worth is the lock.** `backend.Device` is one mutex

input.new_string:
- **Q9b — the VAE's two priced ports, done 2026-09-21 and by the opposite
  route.** conv3x3 was 69.7% of the decode at 3.2 TFLOP/s and the mid
  block's four projections 19.9% at 35 GFLOP/s, both priced as z-image's
  matrix-core kernels reused. `TestConvFP16Ladder` — the instrument the
  ledger itself said to build first — refused that: narrowing every 3x3
  costs the decoded image **max abs 0.178** (23 of 255 8-bit levels) and
  narrowing **one** convolution costs 0.0885, against an fp32 port at
  7.3e-4; the encoder's posterior mode moves 0.23–0.40 against a gate at
  4.7e-5; narrowing the 1x1 shortcuts as well returns NaN. Taken in fp32
  instead, as a register block (OC 8→48 over an LDS slab 4x smaller, 5.12 →
  3.38 s) and a 64x64 tiled GEMM (1.08–1.70 s → **9 ms**), both
  bit-identical: **decode 7.4 → 4.02 s, encoder 1.7 → 0.91 s**. What is left
  in the decode is conv3x3 at 85.9% and 4.9 TFLOP/s, whose remaining ceiling
  is one shared read per multiply-add; a pixel block is priced at ~1.5 s
  more and is the only one of these that would *not* be bit-identical.
  Everything past that is the DiT's, which is now 95% of the image.

content.content:
**Open, in IMAGE.md's order:**

- **Three precision facts to carry into anything that touches this
  vertical**, each of which has already caught a port:
  - **the VAE cannot take fp16 operands anywhere** (Q9b, above). Its tail
    norm is the amplifier, so the rule is not "watch the range" but "do not
    narrow". `TestConvFP16Ladder` is the instrument; re-run it before
    pointing any narrowing kernel at `qimage/vae`.
  - **the vision tower amplifies an input perturbation by ~10³**, so a
    condition image must be quantized exactly as the reference's is —
    compositing alpha over white in float rather than on 8-bit levels moves
    the prompt embedding by rel 11 (a firing control), which is why the
    Lanczos resampler is gated on exact 8-bit equality and not a tolerance.
  - **on a non-square condition image the fp32 dump is the less accurate
    side** — rel 1.4e-3 from a float64 run where the Go tower sits 2.1e-4 —
    so that stage is gated against dumped float64 rows.
- **The 1184² ceiling.** A capability, not a percent: the VAE decoder's
  activation arena is one storage buffer against a 4 GiB − 4 device limit,
  so the model's own 2048² examples do not decode. Tiled decode, or a
  multi-buffer arena (`vk.PipelineSpec.Counts`, the LLM's 77 GB bank is the
  precedent).
- **Q9b — the VAE's two priced ports, done 2026-09-21 and by the opposite
  route.** conv3x3 was 69.7% of the decode at 3.2 TFLOP/s and the mid
  block's four projections 19.9% at 35 GFLOP/s, both priced as z-image's
  matrix-core kernels reused. `TestConvFP16Ladder` — the instrument the
  ledger itself said to build first — refused that: narrowing every 3x3
  costs the decoded image **max abs 0.178** (23 of 255 8-bit levels) and
  narrowing **one** convolution costs 0.0885, against an fp32 port at
  7.3e-4; the encoder's posterior mode moves 0.23–0.40 against a gate at
  4.7e-5; narrowing the 1x1 shortcuts as well returns NaN. Taken in fp32
  instead, as a register block (OC 8→48 over an LDS slab 4x smaller, 5.12 →
  3.38 s) and a 64x64 tiled GEMM (1.08–1.70 s → **9 ms**), both
  bit-identical: **decode 7.4 → 4.02 s, encoder 1.7 → 0.91 s**. What is left
  in the decode is conv3x3 at 85.9% and 4.9 TFLOP/s, whose remaining ceiling
  is one shared read per multiply-add; a pixel block is priced at ~1.5 s
  more and is the only one of these that would *not* be bit-identical.
  Everything past that is the DiT's, which is now 95% of the image.
- **The step count is swept and settled**: 40 stays the default because it
  is the only count safe across prompt kinds. Photographic and painterly
  prompts are convincing at **12 steps (36 s, 36% of the cost)**; a
  structured technical drawing is good at 24 (1m4s) and has come apart by
  12. `steps` is a request field, so a client that knows its prompt can take
  the discount. Re-run with `QI21_SWEEP=1 go test ./qimage/pipeline -run
  TestStepSweep`.
- **Masked edits**: still a 501, but the reason moved — 2.1 *can* do them and
  how a mask is fed is not in the diffusers implementation (IMAGE.md Q-o3).

and height at construction, so a size was a residency question.

It is not one, and none of the three graphs had to change to stop it being
one. The transformer states its run length per image, the VAE re-records its
graph from the latent it is handed and checks the arena rather than assuming
it, and the rotary table is rebuilt per run anyway. So `-image-size` is a
*ceiling* and a default, the way `-max-audio` is for parakeet, and every
smaller image runs in the same arenas. Measured on one 1024x1024 process,
two runs, at the default 40 steps:

| stage | 1024x1024 |
|---|---|
| text encoder | 107 ms / 105 |
| DiT prefill (step 0, which also fills the prefix KV cache) | 2.151 s / 2.163 |
| 39 cached steps, mean | 2.117 s / 2.140 |
| VAE decode | 7.48 s / 7.75 |
| **request** | **1m32.3 s** / 1m33.5 |

**An image is the transformer and almost nothing else**: 91% of that wall
clock is the 40 denoising steps, 8.1% is the VAE and 0.1% is the text
encoder. The two levers are therefore the step count — genuinely per request
here, unlike under a turbo distillation — and the unported percents
`IMAGE.md`'s Q9 prices.

An *edit* at the same size, with one reference image, is **1m58.6 s /
1m59.2**: the reference's own encoding 7.8 s (a 27-layer vision tower and a
VAE encode), text encoding 0.71 s, the prefill 5.19 s against a generation's
2.15, 40 steps at 2.47 s against 2.12, and the same 7.5 s decode. The extra
is the prefix — thousands of rows of reference latents that every step
attends over.

Over HTTP, on a `-image -image-size 512x512 -image-steps 24` process: a
512x512 image at 24 steps comes back in **16.8 s then 14.5 s**, base64 body
included. **The step count is worth sending.** IMAGE.md's sweep (same seed,
three prompt kinds, 1024x1024) found the answer is prompt-dependent rather
than a single number:

| steps | wall | photographic | painterly | structured/technical |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 40 (default) | 1m38 | good | good | good |
| 24 | 1m4 | good | good | good |
| 16 | 45 s | good | good | washed out, structure fragmenting |
| 12 | 36 s | good | good | broken |

(The wall clocks are the sweep's own, taken before Q9's 6% — the ratios are
what it was measuring, and 40 steps is 1m32 today.)

40 is the default because it is the only count safe across all three; **24
is the honest fast setting** at −35% with no visible loss on any of them,
and a client that knows it is asking for a photograph can go to 12 for a
third of the cost.

1	# API — the models behind one HTTP server
2	
3	`cmd/serve` is the long-lived process: an OpenAI-shaped API over the models in
4	this repository, with one flag per vertical deciding what is resident.
5	
6	    go run ./cmd/serve -llm -embed -tts -stt
7	
8	`GOALS.md`'s last line — "we will ultimately serve up a HTTP API serving these
9	features, in Go" — is what this is, and all five verticals are now behind it.
10	
11	The same process has a **second door** for the two speech verticals, because
12	the thing on the other side of a house's microphones does not speak OpenAI:
13	
14	    go run ./cmd/serve -tts -stt -wyoming 0.0.0.0:10300
15	
16	See [Home Assistant speaks Wyoming](#home-assistant-speaks-wyoming-not-openai).
17	
18	## What answers today
19	
20	| Endpoint | State |
21	|---|---|
22	| `GET /v1/models` | **done** — lists what the process actually loaded, with the speech model's voices |
23	| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | **done** — qwen3.8-flash-next, `-llm`, buffered and SSE |
24	| `POST /v1/responses` | **done** — the same generation, OpenAI's newer envelope |
25	| `POST /v1/messages` | **done** — the same generation, Anthropic's envelope |
26	| `POST /v1/audio/speech` | **done** — kokoro, `-tts` |
27	| `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` | **done** — parakeet, `-stt`, with word and segment timings |
28	| `POST /v1/embeddings` | **done** — Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, `-embed`, float or base64, MRL widths |
29	| `POST /v1/images/generations` | **done** — qwen-image-2.1, `-image`, any size the arenas hold, RGBA with `background: "transparent"`, streaming previews with no flag |
30	| `POST /v1/images/edits` | **done** — qwen-image-2.1, `-edits N`, up to N reference images, conditional generation rather than SDEdit (no `strength`) |
31	
32	Every endpoint is *routed*, including the ones that are not implemented: a
33	client gets a 501 that says what is missing and, where a flag would have fixed
34	it, which flag. A 404 would mean a misspelled path and nothing else.
35	
36	## The three packages
37	
38	    cmd/serve   flags, load order, graceful shutdown
39	    backend/    the adapters: weights, device residency, one lock each
40	    api/        routing, request shapes, encoding; imports no model
41	
42	The direction of the dependency is `cmd/serve -> backend -> api`, never the
43	other way. `api` *declares* the backend interfaces (`api.SpeechBackend`,
44	`api.TranscriptionBackend`, `api.CompletionBackend`, `api.EmbeddingBackend`,
45	`api.ImageBackend`) and implements none of them, so it pulls in no checkpoint
46	loader and no Vulkan, and its tests run against fakes in milliseconds —
47	`go test ./api/` needs no `models/` directory and no GPU, including for the
48	three chat envelopes and their streams and for every size the image endpoint
49	resolves.
50	
51	What crosses the boundary is deliberately model-shaped and not
52	container-shaped. A speech backend returns `*audio.Clip` — samples and a rate
53	— and the HTTP layer encodes the WAV or the raw PCM, because which one was
54	asked for is the request's business and not the model's. A transcription
55	backend is handed an already-decoded clip for the same reason in reverse.
56	
57	**The completion backend's signature is a streaming one**, and the buffered
58	response is written in terms of it rather than the other way round. A token
59	on this part costs ~44 ms of the wall clock at 22.7 tok/s, so a 500-token
60	answer is 22 seconds: an interface that returned the whole thing would make
61	the streamed endpoint impossible to build on top of it, where the buffered one
62	is a string builder over the streaming one. That is also what keeps the two
63	answers to the same prompt identical — a server whose streaming path is a
64	separate implementation is a server whose two answers eventually differ, over
65	some whitespace one of them strips.
66	
67	## The log does not keep the conversations
68	
69	`-log-bodies` is off by default, and that default is the point: this server's
70	request and response bodies are its users' prompts and answers, and a process
71	that stays up would otherwise write every one of them to disk as a side effect
72	of having an access log. With it off the log still carries the method, the
73	path, the status, the duration and the sizes — which is what an operator reads
74	anyway. An event stream is never kept whatever the flag says: the first
75	kilobyte of one is a fragment of a frame.
76	
77	## Requests are serialised at the queue
78	
79	A `vk.Device` holds a single queue and nothing in `vk` is externally
80	synchronised, so two requests recording and submitting at once is undefined
81	behaviour rather than contention. `backend.Device` is the device plus the lock
82	that fixes that: every run and every staging pass goes through `Do`, and the
83	server is concurrent at the HTTP layer and serial at the GPU.
84	
85	That is also the only arrangement that makes sense on this part. These models
86	are each sized to saturate the iGPU; two of them interleaved would not go
87	faster, they would share a 236 GB/s bus.
88	
89	## Residency, and the one place it is not resident yet
90	
91	**The language model is resident, and it is most of the machine.** `-llm`
92	stages all 48 layers, the dense banks and the 512-expert bank at startup —
93	**33.5 s**, and the process then holds ~84 GB — so a request is a prefill and
94	one forward pass per token with no weight ever moving again. Two numbers are
95	decided at startup rather than per request: `-llm-ctx`, the attention cache's
96	cell count and so the longest conversation the process can hold, and
97	`-llm-batch`, how many tokens the prefill arenas hold. A conversation past the
98	cache is refused with both numbers rather than truncated at one end; a prompt
99	past the batch is prefilled in chunks of it, which is the same computation by
100	L7b's gate.
101	
102	**The device lock is taken per forward pass and not per request.** A
103	completion is seconds long and the speech models are milliseconds, so holding
104	the queue for a whole generation would make a transcription wait behind it for
105	nothing: between two decode steps there is no work in flight. What is held for
106	the length of a request is the *graph*, whose cache, PLE ring and DeltaNet
107	state are one sequence's — two conversations interleaved in them would not be
108	slower, they would be one conversation.
109	
110	**Parakeet is resident.** `-stt` stages the encoder and the transducer tail
111	once, sized for `-max-audio` seconds (60 by default), and every shorter clip
112	runs in the same arenas — `UploadMel` settles the geometry per run. A request
113	costs a front end on the host and two submits. A longer clip is refused with a
114	message saying what the server was sized for, rather than being truncated.
115	
116	**The embedding model is resident**, and it is the cheapest thing here:
117	`-embed` stages 0.88 GB of fp16 banks in **1.3 s**, and an input then costs
118	**11.5 ms** whatever it says — a 27-token query and an 8-token document take
119	the same time, because at these lengths the run is the weights read once
120	(research/embedding-vertical.md E6). `-embed-tokens` sizes the arenas and is therefore where an
121	input is truncated: the front of the text survives and the end-of-text token
122	is re-appended, because last-token pooling takes *that* row and an input
123	truncated through it would be pooled from an ordinary word.
124	
125	**The image pipeline is resident, and its resolution is not part of what is
126	resident.** `-image` stages 13.2 GB of text encoder, 13.3 GB of transformer
127	and 1.0 GB of VAE in **28 s**, sizes 5.0 GB of activation arenas for
128	`-image-size`, and then a request moves no weight. That last clause is what
129	this endpoint needed and did not have: the pipeline used to fix its width
130	and height at construction, so a size was a residency question.
131	
132	It is not one, and none of the three graphs had to change to stop it being
133	one. The transformer states its run length per image, the VAE re-records its
134	graph from the latent it is handed and checks the arena rather than assuming

systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user restart ai.service

content.text:
Done. The next item was **Q9's remaining ledger — the VAE's two priced ports**, and the instrument it said to build first changed the answer.

## The refusal, measured

The ports were priced as z-image's matrix-core kernels reused (conv3x3 at 69.7% and 3.2 TFLOP/s; the four mid projections at 19.9% and 35 GFLOP/s). `TestConvFP16Ladder` — the CPU decoder run with fp16 conv operands and fp32 accumulators — refused the whole route:

| narrowed | decoded image, max abs |
|---|---|
| nothing (shipped fp32 port) | 0.00073 |
| `conv_in` alone — **one** conv, 0.006% of the arithmetic | **0.0885** |
| every 3x3 | **0.178** (23 of 255 8-bit levels) |
| every conv | **NaN** (up_blocks.4's shortcut reads absmax 2.6e5) |

It's precision, not range, and no exclusion rule helps. The mechanism is the tail norm: the residual stream runs at absmax 1e4–2.6e5 and `norm_out` divides a per-pixel L2 out of it, so a 5e-4 relative perturbation lands as an absolute one at a quiet pixel (rel 1.13 at norm_out). The encoder is worse — its posterior mode moves 0.23–0.40 against a gate at 4.7e-5. z-image's decoder peaks at 497 and has a group norm; the inheritance was never a small extrapolation.

## The same percents, taken in fp32

Both kernels were losing on *shape*, and `TestGPUKernelScreen` (9 arms, each required to decode **byte-for-byte** identically to the pair it replaces):

- **conv2d**: `OC_BLOCK` 8→48 over a 4x smaller LDS slab — 5.12 s → **3.38 s**. The map is not what the argument predicts: raising the register block alone buys nothing (oc8→oc16 at ic32 is 5.12→5.18) and oc32ic32 is the *slowest* arm; LDS footprint governs, and the block only pays once waves stay resident.
- **`qvae_gemm_f32.comp`** (new, 64x64 tile / 4x4 register tile): 1.08–1.70 s → **9 ms**, ~150x. The naive kernel was re-reading the whole weight per row of A.

**Results**, all bit-identical: decode 7.4 → **4.02/4.03 s**, VAE encoder 1.7 → **0.91 s**, served image 1m32.3/1m33.5 → **1m28.8/1m29.8**, served edit 1m58.6/1m59.2 → **1m54.2/1m56.6**. Not one gate moved a digit (decoder 7.3e-4/7.8e-4, GPU-vs-CPU 4.9e-4, encoder mode 2.6e-5/4.3e-5, DupUp control 18443x, served oracles 0.0333/mean 3.4e-4 and 0.0014/mean 1.7e-4).

Two side effects worth knowing: the four 1x1 shortcuts came along free (283 → 63 ms), and `zimage/vae`'s reprieve has expired — it was kept as the test bed for the kernel Q9 turned out not to want. Deleting it now only needs `tensor.go`/`math.go` hoisted; ~8k lines, mechanical, not done here and recorded as such.

Docs rewritten (`IMAGE.md` Q9b + decision 7, `TODO.md`, `API.md`), and the service is redeployed and verified serving a 512²/16 image in 9.5 s.
